summary: Postinstall and import-time beacon exfiltrates host metadata to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package ships a postinstall script (beacon.cjs) that POSTs a JSON payload containing the installer's hostname, install path, current working directory, Node.js version, and package name to a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint over plain HTTP (http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc). The same beacon is invoked at require time from index.js, so the exfiltration fires both on `npm install` (via the postinstall lifecycle hook) and whenever the module is loaded. The package's main entry is an inert Proxy that returns no-op functions for any property access, so the package provides no component functionality matching its `@ppa-web-components/ppa-headerfooter` name; the beacon is the only real behavior. The destination is a bare IP unrelated to any declared publisher or namespace, with no TLS and no caller configuration, consistent with a dependency-confusion fingerprinting / installer-reconnaissance payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
